The Story of Jindas the Steadfast

I bow to Lord Jina, who is free from all faults, and I write the sacred story of merchant Jindas, who firmly practised right faith.

In the ancient and famous city of Pataliputra (Patna), there lived a famous and Jain-devoted merchant named Jindatt. His wife was Jindasi. Jindas, the hero of this story, was their son. Like his mother, Jindas too was a lover of God, pure-hearted, and endowed with many virtues.

Once, Jindas was returning from Suvarnadvip (the Golden Island) with earned wealth toward his city. Some god named Kal had an ancient enmity with Jindas from a past life, and therefore that god wanted to kill him. So while Jindas was sitting on a ship a hundred yojanas wide, the god said, 'Jindas, if you say that Lord Jinendra is nothing and Jain dharma is nothing, then I can let you live. Otherwise, I will kill you.'

Hearing the god's threat, Jindas and others joined their hands and bowed with great devotion to Lord Mahavir. Fearlessly, they said, 'Sinner, we can never say that Lord Jina and his dharma are nothing. Rather, we firmly declare that Lord Jinendra, more radiant than the sun through omniscient knowledge, and his path, worshipped by the world, is supreme. There is no god and no dharma equal to them in the world.' Having said this, Jindas narrated the story of Brahmadata Chakravartin to all present. Hearing that story, everyone's faith became even stronger.

Upon the arrival of this danger to these dharma-loving souls, the throne of the yaksha Anavrat in Uttarkuru trembled. He immediately came and struck Kaladev on the head with his disc with great force, and threw him into the volcanic fire.

The goddess of wealth, Lakshmi, was greatly pleased by the unwavering faith of the ship's people. She came and honoured these dharma-loving souls with great respect and offered them water with devotion. Truly, who does not honour those worthy souls who practise right faith? After this, Jindas and all others returned home safely. The merit born of devotion helped them.

This story teaches that unwavering faith in Lord Jina and his dharma is the greatest protection. Even when threatened with death by a god, Jindas refused to deny his faith. His courage and steadfastness not only saved him but also inspired others. The wise should cultivate such firm faith that no threat can shake it.
